title: Polar metabolomics in human muscle biopsies using LC-MS
author: Schomakers, Hermans, et al.
materials: Ultra-high resolution LC-QTOF MS Impact II

Timing: 8 h
Timing: 3 min per sample

steps.title: Freeze-dry wet muscle tissue
steps.instruction: Freeze-dry 10–15 mg of wet muscle tissue using a freeze‑dryer (e.g., Zirbus Technology VaCo 2) with an 8 h program set to 0.05 bar and –50 °C; pre‑cool the dryer, loosen the tube lid or poke holes in the tube, place the tube in the dryer, then slowly release the vacuum after the run.

steps.title: Transfer freeze‑dried tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer 2–5 mg (aim for 3 mg) of the freeze‑dried muscle tissue into a clean 2 mL Eppendorf™ Safe‑lock tube.

substeps.instruction: Place the clean tube on an analytical balance and tare.
Use a small spatula to break the tissue into smaller pieces and push/twist to homogenize.
Sweep the pieces into the clean tube (or lightly tap the original tube to transfer enough tissue).
Wipe the outside of the tube with a paper towel and record the weight, ensuring the tissue is actually inside the tube.

steps.title: Create two‑phase extraction
steps.instruction: Add 1,000 µL chloroform to the homogenized sample, vortex for 2 min, then centrifuge 10 min at 20,000 × g and 4 °C to separate phases.

steps.title: Isolate polar top layer
steps.instruction: Using a 1 mL pipette, carefully transfer approximately 850 µL of the clear top (polar) layer to a clean 1.5 mL Eppendorf™ tube without disturbing the chloroform layer.

steps.title: Concentrate polar extract
steps.instruction: Place the 1.5 mL tubes in a pre‑heated vacuum concentrator and run for 1.5 h at 60 °C (or until dry), yielding a yellowish‑white residue.

description: The protocol below describes the procedure for polar metabolomics in human muscle biopsies (Janssens et al., 2022), but the same protocol has been successfully applied for human (Remie et al., 2021; Connell et al., 2021; Remie et al., 2020), mouse (van der Stelt et al., 2021; Zapata-Pérez et al., 2021) or rat tissues (brown adipose tissue, white adipose tissue, heart, liver, kidney, brain, placenta, arterial plaque), cultured cells (primary skin fibroblasts, Human Embryonic Kidney (HEK) cells, bronchial epithelial cells, cumulus cells, oocytes, organoids), blood samples (Zapata-Pérez et al., 2021) (serum, plasma, erythrocytes, platelets, peripheral blood mononuclear cells, whole blood, macrophages), other bodily fluids (saliva, sweat, urine, fecal water, bile, cerebrospinal fluid), model organisms (Molenaars et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2020; Gao et al., 2018; Molenaars et al., 2020) (yeast, fruit flies, zebrafish and C. elegans) and culture medium. Additional details on these matrices can be found in Table S1 Sample Matrix Overview.
